provenance: Synthetic clauses composed for this file in the register of freelance service agreements; none copied from a real or published contract and none drawn from backend/eval/corpus/. Each row was reviewed on three lenses (UPL tone, faithfulness to the clause, risk calibration) before landing; tests/test_optimizer_metric.py re-checks the mechanical gates.

labels.clause_type: one of the eight CG8 targets (ml_inference/src/label_map.py)
labels.difficulty: benign | moderate | harsh — how one-sided the clause is against the freelancer
labels.risk_factors: comma-separated noun phrases, or the literal string None
labels.dspy_risk_score: decimal string in [0, 1]; 0.2 ~ mutual NDA, >= 0.8 ~ uncapped indemnity / full IP assignment

split_rule: optimizer.split_examples: last example of each clause_type -> val (16 train / 8 val)

examples.raw_text: Ownership of Deliverables. Upon the Client's payment in full of the invoice covering a given Deliverable, the Contractor assigns to the Client all copyright in that Deliverable in the form delivered. The Contractor retains ownership of all methods, code libraries, templates and other materials created before or outside this Agreement ("Background IP"), and grants the Client a perpetual, non-exclusive licence to use such Background IP solely as embedded in the Deliverables. The Contractor may display the Deliverables in its portfolio and case studies no earlier than ninety (90) days after their first public release.
examples.plain_language_summary: The client gets the copyright in a deliverable only once its invoice is paid in full, and only in the form you handed over. You keep the methods, code libraries, templates and other materials you made before or outside this job; the client may use them only as built into what you deliver, under a permanent, non-exclusive licence. New work made for this job is not carved out, so once it is paid for and assigned you cannot reuse it. You can show the work in your portfolio and case studies 90 days after it first goes public, and if it never goes public, that wait never starts.
examples.risk_factors: portfolio and case-study rights gated on a client-controlled first public release that may never occur, no licence back to reuse components newly created during the engagement, irrevocable copyright transfer of each delivered version once its invoice is paid

examples.raw_text: Assignment. The Contractor hereby assigns to the Client, effective upon creation and irrespective of payment, all right, title and interest in the Deliverables and in any drafts, notes, sketches and derivative materials produced under this Agreement, and waives all moral rights therein to the fullest extent permitted by law. The Client grants the Contractor a revocable, non-exclusive licence to reproduce up to three (3) images of the Deliverables for portfolio purposes, subject to the Client's prior written approval of each image, which approval the Client may withdraw upon thirty (30) days' written notice.
examples.plain_language_summary: Everything you make for this job, including drafts, notes and sketches, becomes the client's the moment you create it, even if the client never pays you. You also give up your moral rights, such as the right to be named as the author, as far as the law allows. For your portfolio you may reproduce up to three images of the work, and only images the client approves in writing beforehand. The client can cancel that portfolio licence, and can also take back its approval of an image with 30 days' written notice.
examples.risk_factors: Title vests irrespective of payment, Assignment effective on creation, Covers drafts, notes and derivative materials, Moral rights waiver, Portfolio licence revocable at the client's discretion, Portfolio use capped at three images subject to prior written approval

examples.raw_text: Proprietary Rights. The Contractor irrevocably assigns to the Company all inventions, works of authorship, software, designs and know-how conceived, developed or reduced to practice during the term and for twelve (12) months thereafter, whether or not created using Company resources and whether or not related to the Deliverables. This assignment extends to the Contractor's pre-existing tools, libraries and frameworks incorporated into any deliverable. No licence, express or implied, is granted back to the Contractor, who shall not reproduce, display or reference any deliverable, including in any portfolio or promotional material. The Contractor shall execute all further documents requested by the Company at the Contractor's own expense.
examples.plain_language_summary: The company owns everything you invent, write, design or build during the contract and for 12 months after it ends. That includes work done with your own resources, work that has nothing to do with the deliverables, and any of your own pre-existing tools, libraries and frameworks you put into a deliverable. You get no licence back, and you cannot copy, show or mention the work, including in a portfolio or promotional material. You also have to sign any further paperwork the company asks for, at your own cost.
examples.risk_factors: Assigns unrelated personal work, 12-month tail after termination, Swallows pre-existing tools and libraries, No licence back, Total portfolio and publicity ban, Further-assurance costs borne by freelancer

examples.raw_text: Client shall pay Contractor a fixed fee of $6,000 per project phase. Contractor shall invoice upon completion of each phase, and Client shall pay each undisputed invoice within fifteen (15) days of receipt. Any amount not paid when due shall accrue interest at one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month until paid. Client shall reimburse pre-approved out-of-pocket expenses on the same fifteen (15) day schedule upon presentation of receipts. If Client terminates a phase already in progress, Client shall pay Contractor for all work performed through the effective date of termination.
examples.plain_language_summary: You get $6,000 for each project phase, and you send an invoice once a phase is finished. The client then has 15 days from receiving the invoice to pay it, but that 15-day duty applies only to invoices the client does not dispute, and the clause does not say how or by when a dispute has to be raised. Anything paid late builds up interest at 1.5% per month. Out-of-pocket costs you cleared in advance are paid back on the same 15-day schedule once you turn in receipts, and if the client stops a phase partway through, it has to pay you for the work you had already done by the stop date.
examples.risk_factors: Payment duty limited to invoices the client does not dispute, No deadline or procedure set for raising a dispute and no duty to pay the undisputed part, Termination pay for work performed has no valuation basis under the fixed per-phase fee, Expenses reimbursed only if pre-approved

examples.raw_text: Contractor shall submit a single consolidated invoice on the last business day of each calendar month covering Services performed during that month. Client shall pay each approved invoice within forty-five (45) days following approval. Client may withhold payment of any line item it disputes in good faith until such dispute is resolved, and no interest shall accrue on withheld or late amounts. Expenses shall be reimbursed only where Client has given prior written approval and shall not exceed $500 in the aggregate per month. Client may terminate on fourteen (14) days' written notice, in which case Contractor's sole compensation shall be for hours logged and approved prior to the notice date.
examples.plain_language_summary: You can bill only once a month, on the last business day, and the client then has 45 days to pay — counted from when it approves the invoice, not from when you send it. The client can withhold any line item it disputes in good faith until that dispute is resolved, and nothing you are owed earns interest, whether it is withheld or paid late. Expenses are repaid only if the client approved them in writing beforehand, and never more than $500 in a month. The client can end the agreement on 14 days' notice, and you are paid only for hours you logged and it approved before the notice date — work you do during those 14 days is not covered.
examples.risk_factors: Mandatory single monthly invoice delaying pay for early-month work to roughly 75 days after performance, Net-45 clock running from client approval rather than invoice date, Client-controlled approval with no deadline to approve, Good-faith dispute withholding at the client's own judgment, No interest on late or withheld amounts, $500 monthly expense cap with prior-written-approval requirement, 14-day termination where compensation stops at the notice date so the notice period is worked unpaid, Hours logged but not yet approved at the notice date going unpaid

examples.raw_text: Client's obligation to pay any invoice is expressly conditioned upon Client's receipt of corresponding payment from the end client, which the parties agree is a condition precedent and not merely a timing mechanism. Approved invoices shall be paid within ninety (90) days after such receipt. Client shall retain ten percent (10%) of each invoice as a holdback, releasable no earlier than six (6) months after final acceptance. No interest, late fee, or cost of collection shall be payable by Client under any circumstances. Client may set off against sums owed to Contractor any amount Client asserts is owed to it, and Contractor waives any right to suspend Services for non-payment.
examples.plain_language_summary: You get paid only if the client is first paid by the end client; the clause makes that a condition, not just a timing rule, so if that money never arrives, your invoice never comes due. After the client is paid, it has 90 days to pay each invoice it has approved, and the clause sets no deadline or standard for approval. The client also keeps 10% of each invoice until at least 6 months after final acceptance, never owes you interest, late fees, or collection costs, and can deduct any amount it says you owe it. You also give up the right to stop work if you are not paid.
examples.risk_factors: Pay-when-paid condition precedent, Discretionary invoice approval with no deadline or standard, Net-90 running from client receipt, 10% holdback held at least 6 months after final acceptance, No interest late fee or collection costs, Unilateral setoff on merely asserted amounts, Waiver of right to suspend work for non-payment

examples.raw_text: Either party may terminate this Agreement for any reason by giving the other party thirty (30) days' prior written notice. Termination shall not affect fees already earned: the Client shall pay the Contractor for all work performed and all pre-approved expenses incurred up to and including the effective date of termination, within fifteen (15) days of that date. The Contractor shall deliver all completed and in-progress work product to the Client upon receipt of that payment. The sections of this Agreement governing confidentiality and payment obligations survive termination.
examples.plain_language_summary: Either side can end this contract for any reason by giving the other 30 days' written notice. If it ends, the client pays you for all work you have done and for pre-approved expenses, within 15 days of the end date. You hand over your finished and in-progress work once that payment reaches you. The confidentiality and payment terms keep applying after the contract is over.
examples.risk_factors: None

examples.raw_text: The Client may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, for convenience upon ten (10) days' written notice. The Contractor may terminate only for the Client's material breach that remains uncured for thirty (30) days after the Contractor's written notice of such breach. On termination for convenience, the Client shall pay the Contractor for milestones formally accepted in writing prior to the termination date; work in progress toward an unaccepted milestone shall be compensated at fifty percent (50%) of that milestone fee. The Contractor waives any claim for lost profits or fees attributable to the unexpired portion of the Term.
examples.plain_language_summary: The client can end this contract, or just part of it, for any reason with 10 days' written notice. You can only end it if the client seriously breaks the agreement and does not fix it within 30 days of your written notice. If the client ends it for convenience, you are paid for milestones it accepted in writing before the end date, but work still in progress toward a milestone not yet accepted is paid at 50% of that milestone's fee. You also give up any claim for lost profits or fees for the rest of the term.
examples.risk_factors: One-sided termination for convenience on 10 days' notice, Client right to cancel part of the scope, Contractor exit limited to uncured material breach, 50% pay for work in progress on unaccepted milestones, Waiver of lost profits for the unexpired term

examples.raw_text: The Client may terminate this Agreement at any time, effective immediately and without notice, in its sole and absolute discretion. Upon such termination the Contractor's right to any unpaid amounts, including invoices already submitted, is extinguished, and the Contractor shall immediately return or destroy all Client materials. The Contractor may not terminate for any reason prior to the end of the Term; any attempted early termination by the Contractor shall constitute a material breach and shall obligate the Contractor to pay the Client an early exit fee equal to thirty percent (30%) of the total Agreement value. For sixty (60) days following termination the Contractor shall provide transition assistance at no charge.
examples.plain_language_summary: The client can end this contract at any moment, with no warning and for any reason it likes. When that happens you lose the right to money you have not been paid yet, including invoices you already sent, and you have to return or destroy all client materials right away. You cannot end the contract early at all, and if you try, that counts as a material breach of the contract and you owe the client an exit fee of 30% of the total contract value. You also owe 60 days of transition help after the contract ends, with no pay for it.
examples.risk_factors: Immediate termination without notice, Forfeiture of submitted invoices, No freelancer right to terminate, Material breach exposure beyond the exit fee, 30% early exit fee, 60 days of unpaid transition work

examples.raw_text: Each party's total liability to the other under this Agreement, whether arising in contract, tort or otherwise, shall not exceed the total fees paid or payable by the Client to the Contractor in the six (6) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. Neither party shall be liable to the other for loss of profit, loss of data, or any indirect or consequential loss. Each party shall cover the other's losses to the extent they arise from its own gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Nothing in this clause limits any liability that cannot lawfully be limited.
examples.plain_language_summary: This clause caps what either side can be made to pay the other at the fees the client paid you, or still owes you, for the six months before the problem started. The same limit runs both ways, and neither side can claim lost profits, lost data, or other knock-on losses. Each side still covers the other's losses to the extent they come from its own serious carelessness or deliberate wrongdoing. The cap does not apply to liability that the law does not let a contract limit.
examples.risk_factors: Obligation to cover the client's losses caused by your own gross negligence or wilful misconduct, Six-month fee cap also limits what you can recover from the client for unpaid fees, Mutual exclusion of lost profits removes your main remedy if the client drops the project

examples.raw_text: The Contractor shall defend and hold the Client harmless from third-party claims arising from the Contractor's breach of this Agreement or from any allegation that the Deliverables infringe a third party's intellectual property rights, excluding claims caused by materials supplied by the Client. Save for the defence obligation above, the Contractor's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed two times (2x) the fees paid in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim. The Contractor shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence throughout the Term and shall furnish a certificate of insurance on request.
examples.plain_language_summary: You have to defend the client from outside claims caused by your breach of this agreement, or by any claim that your work copies someone's intellectual property, and cover the client's losses. A mere accusation of copying sets this off, this duty has no cap, and claims caused by materials the client gave you are left out. Apart from that defence duty, the most you can owe is twice the fees paid to you in the twelve months before the claim. You also have to carry general liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence for the whole term and give the client a certificate of insurance if asked.
examples.risk_factors: Uncapped defence and hold-harmless duty for third-party claims, Defence duty fired by a mere allegation of IP infringement, One-way protection running only to the client, 2x-fee cap that excludes the largest exposure, Mandatory $1000000 insurance policy carried at your own cost

examples.raw_text: The Contractor shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Client, its affiliates, officers and customers from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, fines and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising out of or relating in any way to the Services, regardless of cause and including claims caused in part by the Client's own negligence. This obligation is unlimited in amount and survives termination of this Agreement indefinitely. The Client's total liability to the Contractor shall in no event exceed five hundred dollars ($500). The Client may withhold or offset from any fees otherwise due such amounts as it deems necessary to cover such claims.
examples.plain_language_summary: If any claim touches your work, this clause makes you pay the client's damages, fines, costs and lawyer fees, and defend the client, its affiliates, officers and customers. It applies even when the client's own carelessness helped cause the claim, there is no dollar limit on what you can owe, and the obligation continues forever after the contract ends. The client's own liability to you is capped at $500. The client can also hold back or subtract money from fees it owes you to cover these claims.
examples.risk_factors: Uncapped indemnity, Covers attorney fees, Applies to claims partly caused by the client, Extends to affiliates officers and customers, Survives termination indefinitely, Client liability capped at $500, Client may offset from unpaid fees

examples.raw_text: Each party may receive information from the other that is marked confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential. Each party agrees to use such information only to perform this Agreement and to protect it with the same care it applies to its own confidential information. These obligations continue for two (2) years after this Agreement ends. They do not apply to information that is or becomes public through no fault of the receiving party, was already known to the receiving party, or is independently developed without use of the disclosing party's information. Either party may disclose Confidential Information where required by law, after giving the other party prompt written notice where notice is permitted.
examples.plain_language_summary: You and the client each keep the other's confidential details private, use them only for this contract's work, and guard them with the same care as your own. This covers anything marked confidential, or that a reasonable person would see as confidential, and the duty lasts for two years after the contract ends. It does not cover details that are or become public through no fault of the side holding them, that the side already knew, or that it worked out on its own without using what the other side shared. Either side may also share details when the law requires it, after giving prompt written notice where notice is allowed.
examples.risk_factors: None

examples.raw_text: Contractor acknowledges that all information disclosed by Client, whether written, oral, or observed on Client premises, and whether or not marked confidential, constitutes Confidential Information. Contractor shall not disclose Confidential Information to any third party, including subcontractors, without Client's prior written consent, and shall maintain such confidentiality for five (5) years following termination. Contractor shall not include any deliverable, Client name, or Client logo in any portfolio, case study, or promotional material without Client's prior written approval. If Contractor receives a subpoena or similar demand, Contractor shall notify Client within three (3) business days and shall cooperate, at Contractor's own expense, with any effort by Client to limit or oppose disclosure.
examples.plain_language_summary: This clause binds only you and covers all the client tells or shows you, even things said out loud, seen at its offices, or not marked. You cannot share it with outsiders, even your own subcontractors, without the client's written consent first, and that duty lasts five years after the work ends. You cannot use any deliverable, the client's name, or its logo in a portfolio, case study, or marketing without written approval first, and that ban has no end date. If you get a subpoena or similar demand, you have three business days to tell the client and pay your own costs to help it limit or fight the demand.
examples.risk_factors: One-way obligation with no matching client duty, Broad definition covering oral and unmarked information, Five-year confidentiality tail after termination, Indefinite ban on portfolio use and client credit, Subcontractor disclosure blocked without written consent, Subpoena cooperation costs borne by the freelancer

examples.raw_text: All information of any kind that Contractor receives, observes, or creates in connection with the Services, including information that is publicly available, shall be deemed Confidential Information of Client and shall remain confidential in perpetuity. Contractor shall not disclose the existence of this Agreement or the identity of Client to any person. Contractor agrees that any disclosure causes irreparable harm and shall pay Client liquidated damages of $50,000 per incident, plus Client's attorneys' fees, and shall cover any loss or claim Client suffers as a result. This Section survives termination and is excluded from any limitation of liability in this Agreement.
examples.plain_language_summary: Everything you receive, see, or create for this job counts as the client's secret forever, even if it is already public, and you cannot tell anyone the contract exists or who the client is. If you disclose anything, you owe $50,000 for each incident, plus the client's legal fees, plus any loss or claim the client suffers as a result. You also agree up front that any disclosure causes harm that money cannot fix, which is the kind of harm a court can order you to stop. These duties outlast the contract and are not covered by any liability cap in the agreement.
examples.risk_factors: Perpetual duration, No public-information exception, No legal-compulsion carve-out, $50,000 liquidated damages per incident, Client attorney fees, Open-ended obligation to cover client losses, Pre-agreed irreparable harm supporting an injunction, Carved out of the liability cap, Client identity and engagement cannot be named

examples.raw_text: Contractor shall deliver the items listed in Exhibit A, consisting of a responsive marketing website of up to eight (8) pages, on or before 14 March 2026. Client shall review each deliverable within seven (7) business days of receipt and shall either accept it or provide a single written list of specific, objective deficiencies measured against Exhibit A. Any deliverable not rejected in writing within that period is deemed accepted. The Fee includes two (2) rounds of revisions per deliverable. Work outside Exhibit A shall proceed only under a written change order signed by both parties stating the additional fee and the revised delivery date.
examples.plain_language_summary: This clause requires you to deliver the marketing website in Exhibit A, up to eight pages, by 14 March 2026, and it gives no extra time if the client is slow. The client has 7 business days after getting each item to accept it or send one written list of specific, objective problems measured against Exhibit A. Anything not rejected in writing in that time counts as accepted. Your fee covers two rounds of revisions per item, and work outside Exhibit A needs a written change order signed by both sides that states the extra fee and new delivery date.
examples.risk_factors: fixed 14 March 2026 delivery date with no extension for client-caused delay, no client duty to supply content or other inputs on any timetable, two paid revision rounds per deliverable with no express cap on rejection cycles, no stated paid route for a further in-scope revision round because change orders cover only work outside Exhibit A

examples.raw_text: Contractor shall complete the deliverables described in the Statement of Work. Client shall have ten (10) business days from delivery to evaluate each deliverable and may reject it if, in Client's reasonable judgment, it does not conform to the Statement of Work. Upon rejection, Contractor shall correct the deliverable at no additional charge within five (5) business days and resubmit it for a further review period. The Fee includes up to four (4) rounds of revisions; additional revisions shall be billed at $85 per hour. Client may request minor adjustments reasonably related to the deliverables, and such adjustments shall not constitute a change in scope. No deliverable is accepted until Client provides written acceptance.
examples.plain_language_summary: The client has 10 business days to review each deliverable and may reject it if, in its reasonable judgment, it does not match the Statement of Work. After a rejection, you get 5 business days to fix and resubmit it at no extra charge, and this loop has no stated limit. Your fee covers up to 4 rounds of revisions; extra revisions are billed at $85 per hour. Nothing is accepted until the client accepts it in writing, and requests for minor adjustments reasonably related to the work are not a change in scope.
examples.risk_factors: No deemed acceptance, Open-ended review loop, Client-judged conformance standard, Minor adjustments excluded from change of scope, Free rework within 5 business days

examples.raw_text: Contractor shall perform the Services and any additional tasks Client deems reasonably necessary or incidental to the Services, at no increase in the Fee. Client may reject any deliverable in its sole and absolute discretion, for any reason or no reason, and Contractor shall revise it without limitation and without additional compensation until Client is satisfied. No deliverable shall be deemed accepted by lapse of time. Time is of the essence; for each calendar day a deliverable is late, the Fee shall be reduced by five percent (5%). Client may terminate for convenience at any time and retain all work product delivered or in progress without payment for unaccepted work.
examples.plain_language_summary: The client can add any extra task it thinks is reasonably necessary or incidental to the job, and your fee stays the same. It can reject any piece of work at its sole discretion, for any reason or none, and you keep revising with no limit and no extra pay until it is satisfied. Deadlines are strict: work never counts as accepted just because time passes, and your fee drops 5 percent for each calendar day work is late, with no floor. The client can end the contract at any time, for any reason, and keep all delivered or in-progress work, with no pay for work it has not accepted.
examples.risk_factors: Unpaid scope creep, Sole-discretion rejection with no stated standard, Unlimited free revisions, No acceptance by lapse of time, Uncapped 5% per-calendar-day fee reduction, Termination for convenience with retention of work product and no payment for unaccepted work

examples.raw_text: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Oregon, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. Before commencing any formal proceeding, the parties will attempt in good faith to resolve the dispute through direct discussions for a period of at least thirty (30) days following written notice of the dispute. If the matter remains unresolved after that period, either party may bring an action in the state or federal courts located where the defending party maintains its principal place of business, and each party will bear its own attorneys' fees and costs.
examples.plain_language_summary: Oregon law decides how this contract is read. If a disagreement comes up, both sides first have to try to settle it through direct talks for at least 30 days after one side sends written notice of the dispute. After those 30 days, either side can take the matter to a state or federal court where the side being sued is based, so if you are the one suing the client you would be filing where the client is based, and if the client sues you it would be filed where you are based. Each side pays its own lawyer bills and other legal costs, whoever wins.
examples.risk_factors: cost and travel of having to sue the client in the client's home forum, 30-day waiting period before any court filing, no recovery of your legal fees even if you win

examples.raw_text: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Illinois. Any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement that is not resolved within fifteen (15) days of written notice shall be finally settled by binding arbitration before a single arbitrator, seated in Cook County, Illinois. The parties shall share the arbitrator's fees and administrative costs equally, and each party shall bear its own attorneys' fees. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may bring a claim in small claims court for amounts under $10,000.
examples.plain_language_summary: Illinois law controls this contract, and most disputes are decided by one private arbitrator instead of a judge or jury. If a dispute is not settled within 15 days after written notice, it must be arbitrated in Cook County, Illinois, wherever you happen to be based. Both sides split the arbitrator's fee and the administrative costs evenly, and each side pays its own lawyer, so you cannot recover your legal costs even if you win. Claims worth less than $10,000 can still go to small claims court.
examples.risk_factors: Binding arbitration in place of a court or jury trial, Arbitrator and administrative fees split 50/50, Each side pays its own attorneys' fees with no recovery of costs on an unpaid invoice, Fixed arbitration seat in Cook County

examples.raw_text: This Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of Delaware. Contractor waives any objection to venue and consents to final, binding, confidential arbitration seated in New York, New York, before a single arbitrator selected by Company. Contractor waives any right to a jury trial and any right to participate in a class, collective, or representative proceeding. Contractor shall advance all filing and arbitrator fees and shall reimburse Company's attorneys' fees if Company prevails on any claim or defense. Any claim not brought within ninety (90) days of the event giving rise to it is permanently barred. Company may nonetheless seek injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction.
examples.plain_language_summary: Delaware law applies, and any dispute goes to private, confidential arbitration in New York City before one arbitrator the client picks. The award is final and binding, you give up a jury trial, and you cannot join a class or group claim. You pay all filing and arbitrator fees up front, and if the client wins on any claim or defense you also pay the client's lawyer fees. Any claim by either side not brought within 90 days of the event behind it is barred for good, but the client can still go to court for an order to stop you from doing something.
examples.risk_factors: Client-selected arbitrator, Final binding award with no appeal or court trial, Distant mandatory arbitration venue, Freelancer advances all filing and arbitrator fees, One-way attorney fee shifting, Jury trial waiver, Class and collective action waiver, 90-day claim cutoff, Confidential proceedings, Court carve-out available only to the client

examples.raw_text: Entire Agreement; Severability. This Agreement, together with any Statement of Work signed by both parties, is the complete agreement between the parties on its subject matter and replaces all prior discussions, proposals, and understandings, whether written or oral. It may be amended only by a written document signed by an authorised representative of each party. If a court of competent jurisdiction finds any provision unenforceable, that provision shall be limited or severed only to the minimum extent necessary, and the remaining provisions shall remain in full force and effect. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is deemed an original.
examples.plain_language_summary: The signed agreement plus any Statement of Work both sides signed is the whole deal. Earlier discussions, proposals and understandings no longer count, whether they were written or spoken, so a promise made before signing binds the client only if it was written into those documents. A change to the terms takes effect only if both sides sign a written document. If a court finds one part unenforceable, that part is narrowed or cut only as far as needed and the rest stays in force. You can sign in separate copies, including by electronic signature, and each counts as an original.
examples.risk_factors: loss of pre-contract promises not written into the agreement or a signed Statement of Work, no effect for oral or informal changes to the terms

examples.raw_text: Notices; Assignment. All notices under this Agreement shall be sent by email to the address listed on the signature page and shall be deemed received one (1) business day after transmission, provided no delivery failure message is returned. Either party may update its notice address upon ten (10) days' written notice. Contractor may not assign, delegate, or subcontract any portion of this Agreement without Company's prior written consent, which Company may withhold in its sole discretion. Company may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, reorganisation, or sale of substantially all of its assets, without Contractor's consent.
examples.plain_language_summary: Notices go by email to the address on the signature page, and they count as received one business day after they are sent unless a delivery failure message comes back. Either side can change its notice address by giving 10 days' written notice. You cannot hand off or subcontract any part of the work without the company's written approval, and it can refuse for any reason it likes. The company can transfer this contract to an affiliate or to a buyer in a merger or sale without asking you.
examples.risk_factors: Deemed receipt of emailed notices, One-way assignment right for the company, Subcontracting blocked at the company's sole discretion, Forced performance for an unknown successor

examples.raw_text: Miscellaneous. Company may modify this Agreement at any time by posting revised terms to its contractor portal, and Contractor's continued performance more than five (5) days after posting constitutes acceptance of the revised terms. Contractor waives any right to individual notice of such modification. Company shall be excused from performance, including payment of undisputed fees, for so long as performance is delayed by any cause beyond its reasonable control, including labour disputes, supply interruptions, and internal budget suspension. Contractor shall remain obligated to perform during any such period. Contractor waives the right to trial by jury and to participate in any class or collective action. Any provision held invalid shall be reformed to the maximum extent enforceable against Contractor.
examples.plain_language_summary: The company can rewrite this contract at any time by posting new terms on its portal. If you keep working more than 5 days after a posting, you are treated as having agreed, and you give up the right to be told about a change individually. If anything outside the company's reasonable control delays it, including its own budget suspension, it can stop paying fees it does not dispute, and you must keep working through that period. You also give up the right to a jury trial and the right to join a class or group lawsuit. If a court finds a provision invalid, it is rewritten to the strongest version that still holds against you.
